caption:
Utah really is one of the most stunning places in the entire country!! 😍

If you are planning a trip to this amazing part of the USA, make sure to follow @peekinourjournal and see more bucketlist spots and destinations to have the best time out here ❤️

↩️ Arches National Park- One of the most famous national parks in the country. It boasts amazing natural arches, including Delicate Arch which is Utah’s License Plate Symbol
♦️ Canyonlands National Park- Spectacular park with amazing views! Catching the sunrise at Mesa Arch when it glows red, has to be on your list
🐎 Dead Horse Point State Park- One of the best sunrise spots in Moab, this state park deserves so much more love! The entry fee is $20 and we highly recommend visiting this place on your trip to Moab
🛻 Marlboro Point- This hidden gem is only accessible via a 4x4 vehicle and offers jaw dropping views across deep, rugged canyons
🏜️ Goblin Valley State Park- Red rocks and rugged hoodoos dominate the landscape of this beautiful park. You can purchase a drone permit at the entrance station 
👽 Bentonite Hills- Located near Mars Research station, this otherworldly spot will surely make you feel like you transported to another planet
🏰 Capitol Reef National Park- The least visited National Park in Utah, this destination is a hidden gem.There are stunning views everywhere and park offers some amazing hikes and even world class rappelling!
🪨 Factory Butte- This beautiful monolith overlooks Hanksville and can be seen from the highway. We suggest off roading and getting closer to it as the landscape is just surreal 
🌒 Moon Overlook- Otherworldly landscape which looks so much like the surface of the Moon. Best accessed via a 4x4, this spot is located close to Hanksville

While the aurora borealis is visible across many countries, Norway, Finland and Iceland are often the top choices due to great tourist infrastructure as well as the stunning scenery and culture 😍

📌 Here are some tips for the perfect Northern Lights trip 

📲 Download apps like ‘Aurora’ and follow live cams like ‘Explore’ to get live updates
⛈️ Cloud cover is the main challenge when viewing Northern Lights so using weather apps for identifying regions with low cloud cover is crucial 
🥶 The lights are best visible during the winters in high latitude areas. So layer up and be prepared to face negative temperatures and lots of Snow
🧤 Hand and Toe Warmers are a great accessory to stock up on for this trip
🚗 Driving around to see the lights is the most convenient way if you are confident of driving in harsh winter conditions 
🚐 You do not really need to book tours to see the Northern Lights. If you’d prefer not to drive though, tours are a great option and most generally include hot beverages and snacks!
🔦 Try to stay away from light pollution which dims the aurora

Days 8-9: Saariselkä & Ivalo
Day 10: Inari
Day 11: Levi
Day 12: Ylläs
Day 13: Kemi
Day 14: Return to Rovaniemi

Road‑tripping in Lapland gives you maximum freedom to chase the northern lights, experience the arctic wilderness, and visit smaller villages.

The roads are cleared regularly, BUT... drive slow, watch out for black ice, stay cautious, and book a proper winterized vehicle (studded tyres, heating, snow brush).

If driving in snow worries you, you can still see Lapland by combining trains, buses and occasional taxis or private transfers. 

🧥 What to pack?
Thermal base layers (merino wool works best)
Fleece mid layers
Outer layers - insulated down jacket and snow pants
Waterproof snow boots with grip
Wool socks, balaclava and beanie
Touchscreen gloves and mittens
Warmers
Headlamp and spare batteries
Tripod to capture the aurora (yes, even for your phone)
Power bank and travel adapter

caption:
‼️if you are visiting Venice this year👇🏻 

🤍 Follow for more unique places and travel guides around the world

Getting there

Fly into Venice Marco Polo Airport. From there, you can take a water taxi (expensive but iconic) or the Alilaguna water bus (budget-friendly). 

If you’re coming by train, Venezia Santa Lucia drops you straight into the heart of the city.

Where to stay

If it’s your first time, stay near San Marco or along the Grand Canal so you can walk everywhere early in the morning before crowds take over.

🤍 I stayed at the @stregisvenice and it was an epic experience. One of my favorite moments of staying here was that every evening they carry on a ritual called champagne sabering - where a bottle is opened with a sword (yes, an actual sword) and I actually got to do it myself and then try it 🤍

Things to do

Get lost. Not even kidding! Venice is best experienced with no plan
Wake up early and walk through Piazza San Marco before 8 AM
Take a vaporetto or gondola ride down the Grand Canal
Visit Burano for colorful houses or Murano for glassmaking
Climb the Campanile for one of the best views in the city

What to eat

Skip the tourist places right by the main squares.
Walk a few streets away and look for smaller, local spots.
Try cicchetti (Venetian tapas), fresh pasta, and tiramisu (this is where it was born).
Also, don’t leave without having a spritz by the water.

Things no one tells you ⚠️

Venice is beautiful, but it’s also crowded. Early mornings and late evenings are your best friend
Restaurants near major attractions are often overpriced and not worth it
Pack light! There are a LOT of bridges and no Ubers here
Acqua alta (flooding) can happen, especially in certain months, so check ahead

Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena is the oldest surviving bank on Earth and it’s still operating.

The bank was originally created to help poor citizens borrow money but over time it grew into one of Italy’s most important financial institutions.

But this city isn’t just famous for banking.

Some of the must see things here are 👇🏻 

Piazza del Campo
Siena Cathedral
Torre del Mangia
and the legendary Palio di Siena, a wild medieval horse race held twice a year in the main square

This is…

📍 Siena, Tuscany, Italy

🚗 How to get here

Siena is about 1 hour from Florence and 2.5 hours from Rome.

Car is easiest for a Tuscany road trip but you can take a train too. The station is below the old town so you’ll need a bus or taxi up.

I’ve been to Finnish Lapland more than once, and while the Northern Lights get most of the attention, some of my favorite memories had absolutely nothing to do with the sky.

Here are some more experiences I highly recommend 

❄️ Visit a snow village / ice hotel
Entire rooms, bars and sculptures are rebuilt from snow and ice every winter. Even if you don’t sleep there, go explore one.

🧖🏻‍♀️ Do a proper Finnish sauna
Bonus points if there’s a frozen lake, snow outside or an ice plunge involved. This might be the most Finnish thing you can do.

🏎️ Try ice karting
Basically go-karts on a frozen track and WAY more fun than I expected.

🏔️ Ski above the Arctic Circle
In Levi because you get snowy forests, frozen landscapes and those ridiculously beautiful pastel winter skies.

🛷 Go snowmobiling through the forest
Especially around blue hour when everything starts glowing deep Arctic blue.

🌌 Chase the Northern Lights yourself
Rent a car if you can drive in these conditions, check the cloud cover + aurora forecast and drive somewhere dark away from town. Some of my best aurora nights happened this way with no one around.

‼️Leave room for doing absolutely nothing
Find a cabin, light the fireplace, make something warm to drink and watch the snow fall outside.

📍Finnish Lapland, Finland 🇫🇮

Getting good at finding 12/10 benches.

But this one might have ruined every future bench for me.

You’re sitting nearly 1,800m above the Salzkammergut with mountains stacked behind mountains and lakes scattered through the valleys below and you barely have to hike for this view.

🚂 How to get here
Take the SchafbergBahn from St. Wolfgang. The cog railway has been climbing Schafberg since 1893 and reaches the top in around 35 minutes.

🏔️ At the top
Don’t immediately head back down. Walk around the summit area because the view changes completely depending on which side you’re standing on. On a clear day, you get a full 360° panorama across the lakes and Austrian Alps.

Give yourself enough time at the summit. THIS is definitely not a “get off, take one photo, leave” kind of stop.

📍Schafberg, St. Wolfgang, Austria

caption:
‼️You don’t always need a car to explore European towns. There are plenty of car-free villages that can only be explored on foot for the most part

🤍 follow for more unique places around the world @tripuntraveled 

Here are 5 car free places in Europe worth adding to your list

🏔️ Zermatt, Switzerland
A mountain village beneath the Matterhorn where regular cars are not allowed. Explore the center on foot, then take the mountain trains and cable cars for some of the most dramatic views in Switzerland.

🚤 Giethoorn, Netherlands
Known for its canals, tiny bridges, and thatched cottages. The old village is best explored by walking along the narrow paths or taking a small boat through the canals.

🏰 Pérouges, France
A medieval hilltop village filled with uneven cobblestones, stone houses, and streets that feel almost untouched by time. Come early.

🌿 Pienza, Italy
A small Renaissance town overlooking the rolling hills of Val d’Orcia. Walk the panoramic streets, stop for pecorino cheese, and stay for sunset over the Tuscan countryside.

🌸 Óbidos, Portugal
A whitewashed medieval town wrapped inside castle walls. Walk through the flower covered streets, walk along the walls, and try the local cherry liqueur served in a chocolate cup.

They say heaven is above the clouds.

But here, it feels like Switzerland tucked an entire village beneath them.

If you’re visiting Lauterbrunnen, don’t just stop at the main viewpoint and leave.

Walk through the valley to Staubbach Falls, continue toward Trümmelbach Falls (the only glacier-fed waterfalls inside a mountain that you can actually explore), then take the cable car up to Grütschalp or Mürren for the panoramic views back over the valley.

If you have extra time, drive or take the train to Wengen on the opposite side for an entirely different perspective. The valley looks completely different from above.

Give yourself at least a full day here.

📍Lauterbrunnen, Switzerland
